The federal division of Chugach Alaska Corporation, CGS has been supporting critical missions as a government contractor for over 25 years. Our focus is to support facility maintenance, IT/technical services, construction and education. We are proud to have built, and continue to foster, an incredibly talented team spanning across the globe in hundreds of different fields – each team member proud to serve our country with first-class business services, while also making a difference for our Chugach shareholders. At CGS, empowering employees is a part of our core, and that focus is one of the ways we build and foster high-performing teams. We empower our employees through competitive compensation and benefits package, professional growth opportunities, truthful communication, and more! If you are looking for an opportunity to serve something bigger than yourself; if you want your day job to be one that creates meaningful value; if you are looking for an environment that highly values employees and respects individual differences – then Chugach Government Solutions may be the right fit for you! Position Location Remote position with regular travel required, up to 50%. Job Overview The Director of Education Operations provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for Chugach Government Solutions’ portfolio of Job Corps Centers. This role is responsible for driving program performance, operational consistency, contractual and regulatory compliance, student outcomes, and strong customer relationships across the Job Corps portfolio. The Director leads and supports Center Directors, partners closely with corporate and operational support functions, and serves as a key liaison with U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) stakeholders. This position also plays an integral role in business growth, contract transitions, recompetes, and the successful integration of additional Job Corps Centers as the portfolio expands. Responsibilities Essential Job Duties: Portfolio Leadership: Provide strategic and operational leadership across the Job Corps portfolio, ensuring consistent execution, strong performance, and alignment with organizational and contractual objectives. Center Director Leadership: Lead, coach, and support Center Directors by establishing clear performance expectations, promoting accountability, and providing guidance to address operational challenges and opportunities. Program Performance: Monitor center and portfolio performance, identify risks, trends, and opportunities, and drive improvement strategies related to student outcomes, operational effectiveness, and contract performance in alignment with the Department of Labor center directives. Budget and Financial Oversight: Provide oversight and support for budgeting, cost management, and effective resource allocation across Job Corps contracts in order to meet the annual financial performance goals. Compliance and Risk Management: Ensure center operations comply with Job Corps requirements, applicable state and federal regulations, contractual obligations, and company policies and procedures. Customer and Stakeholder Relations: Build and maintain strong, collaborative relationships with Job Corps Regional Directors, Contracting Officer’s Representatives (CORs), and other Department of Labor and government stakeholders. Maintain additional collaborative relationships with other Job Corps Operators and regularly participate in industry organizations such as NJCA. Student Success: Champion strategies and initiatives designed to improve student retention, academic achievement, career readiness, completion, placement, and other key student outcomes. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Human Resources, Finance, Contracts, Business Development, Legal, Safety, and other corporate support functions to strengthen center operations and resolve complex business and operational issues. Growth and Transitions: Support Job Corps proposals and recompetes, new contract transitions, and the integration and stabilization of new centers within the portfolio. Continuous Improvement: Promote operational consistency, shared resources, best practices, process improvements, and efficiencies across the Job Corps portfolio. Supervisory Responsibilities: Directly supervise Job Corps Center Directors and may supervise additional portfolio-level support personnel. Job Requirements Mandatory: Bachelor’s degree in Education, Business Administration, Public Administration, or a related field. Minimum of five (5) years of progressive leadership experience working in or supporting Job Corps Center operations. Minimum of two (2) years of direct Job Corps leadership experience at the Center Director level or in a comparable center-level leadership role. Demonstrated ability to manage progressive disciplinary actions through personnel management plans. Strong knowledge of Job Corps program requirements, performance expectations, policies, and applicable federal requirements. Demonstrated experience leading senior managers and/or geographically dispersed teams. Experience with budget management, financial oversight, and resource allocation. Demonstrated ability to assess program performance, identify operational risks, and implement effective improvement strategies. Strong leadership, communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills. Ability to develop and maintain effective relationships with government customers and internal business partners. Ability to travel up to 50%. Preferred: Master’s degree in Education, Business Administration, Public Administration, or a related field. Significant leadership experience within Job Corps operations, including responsibility for center-level performance and outcomes. Experience working directly with U.S. Department of Labor and Job Corps stakeholders. Experience with Firm Fixed Price contracts and federal government contracting, including contract performance and compliance. Experience supporting proposals, recompetes, contract transitions, and/or the integration of new Job Corps Centers. Disclosures Chugach Government Solutions is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, pregnancy, disability, genetic factors, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law. Chugach will provide reasonable accommodations, according to applicable state and federal laws, to all qualified individuals with physical or mental disabilities. In compliance with the ADA Amendments Act (ADAAA), if you have a disability and would like to request an accommodation in order to apply for a position with Chugach Government Solutions or any of its subsidiaries, please email ada@chugachgov.com. Chugach Government Solutions supports pay transparency and is committed to equitable and competitive compensation practices. Compensation for this role will be determined based on factors including job responsibilities, experience, skills, internal equity, geographic location, and applicable contract requirements. Where required by law, compensation ranges will be provided to candidates during the hiring process. Privacy Policy for California Job Applicants

review_candidates.company: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies - IFRC
review_candidates.location: Global Village, Dubai, United Arab Emirates
review_candidates.description: Organizational Context The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe. The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. In Afghanistan, the IFRC supports Afghan Red Crescent Society (ARCS) to deliver community-based health services, including routine immunization and polio vaccination, with outreach activities particularly targeting hard-to-reach and underserved areas. Immunization remains a critical public health priority in Afghanistan. While progress has been made, significant gaps persist in: Routine immunization (RI) coverage Identification and reach of zero-dose children Access in remote and insecure communities Afghanistan is one of the last countries where wild poliovirus transmission remains endemic, making polio eradication a global priority. Aligned with IFRC’s Health and Care Framework 2030, particularly the pillars on Global Health Security and Universal Health Coverage, IFRC seeks to strengthen its contribution to immunization outcomes through scalable, community-based approaches. IFRC And ARCS Are Uniquely Positioned To Contribute Through Community trust and acceptance Volunteer-based outreach networks Last-mile service delivery capacity To support strategic engagement with key donors, IFRC intends to develop a robust, evidence-based business care for scaling up polio eradication and routine immunization activities in Afghanistan. Job Purpose The overall objective of this consultancy is to develop a comprehensive, and donor-ready business case for scaling up for Polio Eradication and Routine Immunization specific to Afghanistan. The Business Case Will Define IFRC and ARCS comparative advantage Identify priority geographies and populations Present scalable delivery models Include a clear financial and investment framework Support resource mobilization and strategic partnerships Job Duties And Responsibilities Scope of work: The Consultant Will Undertake The Following Components Situational analysis Review Afghanistan’s immunization landscape (polio and RI) Analyse coverage trends, zero-dose populations, and inequities Identify key barriers Map key actors Value proposition of IFRC and ARCS Analyze the role of ARCS in community-based service delivery Define the comparative advantage of ARCS Demonstrate complementarity with national EPI and partners Design of scale-up model Identify priority geographies and populations Define intervention packages (e.g. outreach, social mobilization, community engagement) Develop delivery models for scale-up Include implementation modalities and operational considerations Financial and economic analysis Develop costing scenarios Assess cost-effectiveness and value for money Outline funding requirement and resource gaps Impact projection Increased coverage rates Reduction in zero-dose children Contribution to polio eradication goals Consultancy Deliverables This deliverable aims to support strategic engagement between IFRC leadership and donors, positioning IFRC and the Afghan Red Crescent Society (ARCS) as partners of choice for Polio Eradication and Routine Immunization in Afghanistan. The business case will articulate the unique value and comparative advantage of ARCS’ last-mile delivery model. It will provide evidence of alignment with the national Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI), identify priority geographies, and set out measurable coverage targets for scale-up. The deliverable will also outline the resources and investments required for IFRC and ARCS to effectively expand their immunization programming. The Consultancy Will Produce The Following Outputs Inception report Draft business case Validation workshop Final business case and financial model Support To The Consultancy The consultant will work mainly with the Afghanistan country team with support from the Health and Care and Strategic Partnerships and Resource Mobilization teams in the Asia Pacific Regional Office and Geneva office. Time allocation: It is estimated the consultancy will be 60 billable / working days until 28 February 2027. Location: All work can be completely remote from the consultant’s home location. Competencies, Values and Comments Application Instruction Please submit your application in English only .

review_candidates.description: About Soccerment Soccerment Group is a football intelligence company born in Italy and active in more than 50 countries. Following the integration of SICS in 2025, we combine SICS's long-standing video analysis expertise with Soccerment's AI and wearable technology, working with clubs, academies, leagues and federations. Our portfolio includes SICS Atlas, an AI-powered video and data platform for match analysis and scouting, and XSEED, smart wearables (shin guards and GPS trackers) that capture football-specific performance data at scale. The role You will build and own our presence in France, reporting to our Chief Sales Officer. Your market is French football from Ligue 1 to National, plus academies, the league and the federation. The role is fully remote: you work from France, organise your own calendar and travel to clubs as needed. You will: •      Run the French pipeline end to end: prospecting, discovery, demos, negotiation, closing, renewal. •      Start from your existing network of sporting directors, recruitment cells, performance and video analysis staff, and expand it. •      Run demos of SICS Atlas and XSEED, with our data intelligence team supporting you on tailored analyses and case studies. •      Own quarterly revenue targets, keep the CRM clean and produce forecasts we can plan on. •      Bring market feedback to Product: what French clubs need, how they buy, who else they talk to. •      Represent Soccerment at French football events and within the coaching, scouting and performance communities. Hand new clients over to onboarding and support, and stay close to them through renewal. What we look for •      French at native level (C2) and professional English. •      3+ years selling technology to French football clubs, leagues or federations, ideally match analysis and scouting software and/or GPS or EPTS systems. Experience in other markets is welcome, but French football is where you need to have sold before. •      A demonstrable client portfolio in France: an active network of decision-makers at professional clubs and institutions, and a track record you can walk us through (deals closed, renewals, references). •      Comfortable running the full cycle alone, from first call to signed contract. •      Structured pipeline management: you forecast with data, not only instinct. •      Based in France and available to travel across the country. Nice to have •      Italian speaker. •      Experience selling both software subscriptions and hardware. •      A background as a video or performance analyst, scout or coach, so you understand the buyer's day. What we offer •      Fixed remuneration based on your experience and portfolio, plus commissions on the revenue you close. •      100% remote work, with full ownership of your market and your calendar. •      A portfolio that lets you sell to the sporting director, the coaching staff and the academy in one conversation. •      A small team with direct access to the CSO and the co-CEOs, where your market feedback reaches the product roadmap. How we hire All steps are remote. 1.    Intro call with our CSO (30 minutes). 2.   Portfolio and pitch session (60 minutes): how you would approach a Ligue 2 club with SICS Atlas and XSEED, and a walkthrough of your track record in France. 3.   Conversation with the co-CEOs. 4.   References, including at least one former client.
